**Answer.** If one party fails to provide what is necessary for the other party to perform their promise, the contract becomes voidable at the option of the party who is prevented from performing their promise. This party is also entitled to compensation for any loss sustained due to the non-performance of the contract.

**Why.** When a contract involves reciprocal promises, and one party fails to provide what is necessary for the other party to perform, the contract becomes voidable at the option of the party who is prevented from performing. Furthermore, the party who is prevented is entitled to compensation for any loss they have suffered because of the non-performance of the contract.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §53

items.q: What is the intended consequence of destroying or damaging a place of worship that is likely to be considered an insult to a particular religion?
items.ref: The person is likely to consider such destruction, damage or defilement as an insult to their religion.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The person found guilty may be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with a fine, or with both.

**Why.** The destruction or damage to a place of worship, if done with the intention of insulting a particular religion, is considered a serious offense aimed at maintaining communal harmony and religious respect.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §254

A2.t:
**Answer.** The intended consequence is punishment with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

**Why.** The statute aims to protect places of worship and objects held sacred from destruction, damage, or defilement that could be considered an insult to a particular religion. Such actions are deemed criminal offenses with specified penalties to deter such behavior and uphold religious sensitivities.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §298

A3.t:
**Answer.** The act is intended to insult any religion.

**Why.** The law addresses the destruction or damage of a place of worship with the specific intent of insulting any religion. This intent is a necessary element for the offense.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §291

A4.t:
**Answer.** The intended consequence is to insult the religion of any class of persons, or to cause any class of persons to consider the destruction, damage, or defilement as an insult to their religion.

**Why.** The law targets those who destroy, damage, or defile a place of worship with the specific intent of insulting the religion of any class of persons, or with the knowledge that any class of persons is likely to consider such action as an insult to their religion.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §298

items.q: What is the key factor that determines whether an offender is liable to multiple punishments for separate acts that together constitute an offence?
items.ref: The Court which tries him could award for any one of such offences.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The key factor is whether the separate acts are part of a single criminal intent or plan.

**Why.** Under the principle of absorbed offences, if the separate acts are part of a single criminal intent or plan, the offender is liable to only one punishment for all the acts. This prevents the imposition of multiple punishments for acts that are merely incidental to a single criminal purpose.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** The key factor is whether the separate acts combine to form a different offence.

**Why.** If the separate acts combine to form a different offence, the offender can be punished for both the new offence and the individual acts. This ensures that the offender is not punished more than once for the same act, in accordance with the principle of legality.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §9

A3.t:
**Answer.** The offender must be liable to punishment for each of the acts separately.

**Why.** The law requires that the offender must be liable to punishment for each of the acts separately. This liability is the prerequisite for determining if the offender can be punished for all the acts.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §51

A4.t:
**Answer.** The offender is not liable to more than one punishment for the entire offence, unless the law provides otherwise.

**Why.** The law dictates that if an act constitutes an offence, and that act is made up of parts, the offender is not liable to more than one punishment for the entire offence. This limitation applies unless the law specifically provides otherwise.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §9

items.q: What is the legal mechanism by which delivery to a bailee may be made?
items.ref: The delivery to a bailee may be made by doing anything which has the effect of putting the goods in the possession of the intended bailee or of any person authorized to hold them on his behalf.

A1.t:
**Answer.** Delivery to a bailee may be made by delivering the goods to the bailee or to some other person authorized by the bailor to receive the goods on his behalf.

**Why.** The legal mechanism for delivery to a bailee is established to ensure that the transfer of possession of goods is properly documented and recognized under contract law. This ensures that the bailee has lawful possession of the goods as per the terms of the bailment agreement.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** Delivery to the bailee may be made by doing anything which has the effect of putting the goods in the possession of the intended bailee or of any person authorized to hold them on his behalf.

**Why.** The law specifies that the method of delivery to a bailee can be achieved through various means, as long as it results in the actual possession of the goods by the intended bailee or an authorized representative.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §149

A3.t:
**Answer.** Delivery can be made either by the bailor or by the bailee.

**Why.** The law provides that delivery of goods to a bailee can occur in two ways: it can be done by the bailor, or it can be done by the bailee.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §150

A4.t:
**Answer.** Delivery can be made by doing anything that has the effect of putting the goods in the possession of the intended bailee or of any person authorized to hold them on his behalf.

**Why.** The law defines delivery broadly, stating that it occurs when an act is performed that puts the goods in the possession of the bailee or any authorized person. This action must be done in relation to the goods that were originally bailed.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §149

items.q: What is the legal relationship between the person who furnishes necessaries and the incapable person to whom they are supplied?
items.ref: The person who furnishes necessaries is entitled to be reimbursed from the property of the incapable person, establishing a debt-recovery relationship.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The person who furnishes necessaries is entitled to a lien on the property of the incapable person for the value of the necessaries supplied.

**Why.** This legal relationship arises under the principle that a person who supplies necessaries to an incapable individual (such as a minor or an insane person) has a right to be paid for those necessities, and can retain possession of the property until payment is made.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §56

A2.t:
**Answer.** The person who furnishes necessaries is entitled to be reimbursed from the property of the incapable person to whom they are supplied.

**Why.** This legal relationship arises when a person, who is either incapable of entering into a contract or someone legally bound to support them, receives necessaries suited to their condition in life. The supplier of these necessaries can claim reimbursement from the incapable person's property to recover the cost of the supplies provided.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §68

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person who supplies necessaries is legally bound to furnish them to the incapable person.

**Why.** The law establishes that whoever supplies necessaries to an incapable person is legally bound to do so. This binding obligation applies regardless of whether the supply is made for the person's own benefit or for the benefit of another person.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §145

A4.t:
**Answer.** The person who supplies necessaries is entitled to be reimbursed from the property of the incapable person.

**Why.** The law establishes that when a person supplies necessaries to someone who is legally incapable of contracting or who is legally bound to be supported, the supplier is entitled to reimbursement from the property of that person.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §68

items.q: What is the legal status of a person who is a member of an unlawful assembly that commits an offence in prosecution of its common object?
items.ref: That person is guilty of the offence committed.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A person who is a member of an unlawful assembly that commits an offence in prosecution of its common object can be tried and punished as an accomplice.

**Why.** The law considers such individuals as accessories to the crime committed by the unlawful assembly, thereby subjecting them to the same legal consequences as principal offenders.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** Such a person is guilty of the offence committed by the unlawful assembly.

**Why.** According to the statute, if an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in pursuit of the common object of that assembly, every person who is a member of the assembly at the time of the offence is equally guilty of that offence.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §190

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be deemed to have committed the offence.

**Why.** A person who is a member of an unlawful assembly and commits an offence in prosecution of its common object shall be deemed to have committed the offence.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §154

A4.t:
**Answer.** Every person who is a member of the unlawful assembly at the time of the commission of the offence is considered guilty of that offence.

**Why.** The law establishes that if an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly while pursuing the common object of that assembly, or if the members know it is likely to be committed, then every member present at the time of the offence is guilty of that offence.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §190

items.q: What is the legal status of a public servant who engages in trade when they are not supposed to?
items.ref: The public servant shall be punished as stated in the provision.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A public servant who engages in trade when prohibited is guilty of an offense.

**Why.** Engaging in trade by a public servant while prohibited constitutes a breach of their duty and trust, and is therefore considered an offense under the law.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** A public servant who engages in trade when legally bound not to do so will be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both, or with community service.

**Why.** This provision outlines the specific legal consequences for public servants who violate their duty by engaging in trade, emphasizing the importance of adhering to professional ethics and legal obligations.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §202

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term that may extend up to two years, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Why.** A public servant who trades while prohibited is punishable with imprisonment up to two years, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §194

A4.t:
**Answer.** Such a public servant shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term up to one year, or with fine, or with both, or with community service.

**Why.** The law mandates that any public servant who engages in trade while legally bound not to do so shall face punishment. This penalty includes simple imprisonment up to one year, fine, or community service.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §202

items.q: What is the maximum amount of bond that can be fixed under this Chapter?
items.ref: The amount of every bond shall not be excessive.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum amount of bond that can be fixed under this Chapter is ten times the estimated value of the property in dispute.

**Why.** This provision ensures that the bond set by the court is sufficient to cover the potential damages or losses arising from the breach of contract, thereby protecting the interests of the aggrieved party.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §56

A2.t:
**Answer.** The amount of every bond executed under this Chapter shall not be excessive and shall be fixed with due regard to the circumstances of the case.

**Why.** The law aims to ensure that the bond amount is fair and not overly burdensome, reflecting the specific circumstances of each case to prevent exploitation.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §484

A3.t:
**Answer.** The bond cannot exceed one thousand rupees.

**Why.** The bond amount must not exceed one thousand rupees.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §185

A4.t:
**Answer.** The amount of every bond must be fixed with due regard to the circumstances of the case and shall not be excessive.

**Why.** The law mandates that the amount of every bond executed under this Chapter must be fixed with due regard to the circumstances of the case and shall not be excessive.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §484

items.q: What is the maximum duration of imprisonment that a Magistrate may award in default of payment of fine, if the defendant has already been sentenced to imprisonment for the same offense?
items.ref: One-fourth of the term of imprisonment which the Magistrate is competent to inflict as punishment for the offence otherwise than as imprisonment in default of payment of the fine.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A Magistrate may award a maximum of six months' additional imprisonment in default of payment of fine if the defendant has already been sentenced to imprisonment for the same offense.

**Why.** The statute aims to ensure that the additional penalty of imprisonment for non-payment of fine does not exceed the original term of imprisonment imposed for the offense.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §154

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum duration of imprisonment that a Magistrate may award in default of payment of fine cannot exceed one-fourth of the term of imprisonment which the Magistrate is competent to inflict as punishment for the offence otherwise than as imprisonment in default of payment of the fine.

**Why.** This limitation ensures that the additional imprisonment for non-payment of fine does not unduly extend the total sentence beyond the original maximum term of imprisonment the Magistrate can impose for the offense.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §24

A3.t:
**Answer.** The Magistrate may sentence the person to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months.

**Why.** If the person has already been sentenced to imprisonment for the offence, the Magistrate may sentence him to imprisonment for a term which shall not exceed six months.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §459

A4.t:
**Answer.** The term of imprisonment cannot exceed one-fourth of the term of imprisonment which the Magistrate is competent to inflict as punishment for the offence otherwise than as imprisonment in default of payment of the fine.

**Why.** The law limits the term of imprisonment that can be awarded in default of payment of fine. This limitation applies specifically when the defendant has already been sentenced to imprisonment for the same offense. The maximum term cannot exceed one-fourth of the term of imprisonment which the Magistrate is competent to inflict as punishment for the offence otherwise than as imprisonment in default of payment of the fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §24

items.q: What is the maximum duration of imprisonment that can be imposed for the offence of bribery?
items.ref: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum duration of imprisonment that can be imposed for the offence of bribery is seven years.

**Why.** The statute sets out specific penalties for various crimes, including bribery, where the perpetrator is liable to imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and/or a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum duration of imprisonment that can be imposed for the offence of bribery is one year.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the punishment for bribery includes imprisonment for a term that may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. The maximum term of imprisonment is thus limited to one year.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §173

A3.t:
**Answer.** The offender may be sentenced to imprisonment for a term which may extend up to seven years.

**Why.** The law mandates that the punishment includes imprisonment for a term extending up to seven years. This is the maximum penalty available for the offence.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §174

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum duration of imprisonment for the offence of bribery is one year.

**Why.** The law specifies that whoever commits the offence of bribery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §173

items.q: What is the maximum duration of simple imprisonment that a public servant may receive for negligently allowing a person to escape from confinement?
items.ref: Two years

A1.t:
**Answer.** A public servant may receive a maximum of two years of simple imprisonment for negligently allowing a person to escape from confinement.

**Why.** The statute limits the liability of public servants to ensure they do not face excessive penalties for minor negligence, while still holding them accountable for their duties.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §95

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum duration of simple imprisonment that a public servant may receive for negligently allowing a person to escape from confinement is two years.

**Why.** The statute specifies that for negligent actions, the punishment includes simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §261

A3.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment is six months.

**Why.** The law specifies that the punishment involves imprisonment which may extend up to six months. This penalty applies when the public servant acts negligently and allows a person to escape from their lawful custody.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §174

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum duration of simple imprisonment is two years.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever, being a public servant, negligently suffers a person to escape from confinement shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §261

items.q: What is the maximum fine that can be imposed for refusing to sign a statement when required to do so by a public servant?
items.ref: Three thousand rupees

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum fine that can be imposed for refusing to sign a statement when required to do so by a public servant is Rs. 200.

**Why.** This provision aims to ensure compliance with official requests for statements while imposing a deterrent through fines. The specific amount is set to balance the need for cooperation with the protection of individual rights.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §95

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum fine that can be imposed for refusing to sign a statement when required to do so by a public servant is three thousand rupees.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the punishment includes simple imprisonment for up to three months, a fine up to three thousand rupees, or both. The maximum fine is thus capped at three thousand rupees.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §215

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with a fine, or with both.

**Why.** The law mandates that the punishment includes imprisonment up to six months, or a fine, or both. This penalty applies to any person who refuses to sign a statement after being required to do so by a public servant.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §231

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum fine for this offense is three thousand rupees.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever refuses to sign a statement when required to do so by a public servant legally competent to require that signing shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to three months, or with a fine up to three thousand rupees, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §215

items.q: What is the maximum fine that can be imposed for the offense of obstructing a public servant in the discharge of their public functions?
items.ref: Fine which may extend to two thousand and five hundred rupees.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum fine that can be imposed for the offense of obstructing a public servant in the discharge of their public functions is Rs. 1,000.

**Why.** The statute sets out the penalties for various offenses, including obstruction of a public servant, and specifies the maximum fine that can be levied for such an offense.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §154

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum fine that can be imposed for the offense of obstructing a public servant in the discharge of their public functions is two thousand and five hundred rupees.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the punishment for obstructing a public servant includes imprisonment for up to three months, a fine not exceeding two thousand and five hundred rupees, or both. The maximum fine is thus clearly defined in the provision.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §221

A3.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment up to six months, or with a fine up to five thousand rupees, or with both.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with a fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §194

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum fine that can be imposed is two thousand and five hundred rupees.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever voluntarily obstructs any public servant in the discharge of his public functions shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term up to three months, or with fine up to two thousand and five hundred rupees, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §221

items.q: What is the maximum fine that can be imposed on someone who knowingly or negligently omits to take measures to guard against probable danger to human life from the fall of a building?
items.ref: Five thousand rupees

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum fine that can be imposed is Rs. 10,000.

**Why.** The statute aims to ensure public safety by mandating necessary precautions to prevent accidents. The prescribed fine acts as a deterrent to encourage compliance with safety regulations.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum fine that can be imposed is five thousand rupees.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the punishment includes a fine which may extend to five thousand rupees for failing to take necessary measures to guard against probable danger to human life from the fall of a building.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §290

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment up to six months, and in addition to this imprisonment, the offender is also liable to a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §279

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum fine that can be imposed is five thousand rupees.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever commits this offense shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term up to six months, or with a fine up to five thousand rupees, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §290

items.q: What is the maximum fine that may be imposed on an offender who knowingly or negligently conveys a person by water in an unsafe or overloaded vessel?
items.ref: The maximum fine is five thousand rupees.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum fine that may be imposed on an offender is Rs. 500.

**Why.** This penalty is designed to deter unsafe practices in water transportation and ensure public safety. Offenders found guilty of conveying persons in unsafe or overloaded vessels can face fines up to Rs. 500 to penalize their actions.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §124

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum fine that may be imposed on an offender who knowingly or negligently conveys a person by water in an unsafe or overloaded vessel is five thousand rupees.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the punishment includes imprisonment for up to six months, a fine of up to five thousand rupees, or both. The maximum fine is thus limited to five thousand rupees.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §284

A3.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to a fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, and they are also liable to a fine. This punishment applies when the offender knowingly or negligently conveys a person by water in an unsafe or overloaded vessel.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §278

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum fine that may be imposed is five thousand rupees.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever knowingly or negligently conveys a person by water in an unsafe or overloaded vessel shall be punished with imprisonment up to six months, or with a fine up to five thousand rupees, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §284

items.q: What is the maximum level of Magistrate authorized to grant a warrant to search for a document, parcel, or other thing in the custody of the postal authority?
items.ref: A District Magistrate or Chief Judicial Magistrate.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A Metropolitan Magistrate is authorized to grant a warrant to search for a document, parcel, or other thing in the custody of the postal authority.

**Why.** The power to issue search warrants is vested in magistrates of a certain level to ensure proper oversight and compliance with procedural requirements. A Metropolitan Magistrate, being of higher rank, is capable of handling such requests due to the nature and scope of their jurisdiction.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §154

A2.t:
**Answer.** A District Magistrate or Chief Judicial Magistrate is authorized to grant a warrant to search for a document, parcel, or other thing in the custody of the postal authority.

**Why.** This authority is specifically granted to District Magistrates and Chief Judicial Magistrates according to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §95(3).

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §95(3)

A3.t:
**Answer.** The warrant may be issued by any Magistrate of the first class.

**Why.** A warrant to search for a document, parcel, or other thing in the custody of the postal authority can only be issued by a Magistrate of the first class.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §174

A4.t:
**Answer.** A District Magistrate or Chief Judicial Magistrate is the only Magistrate authorized to grant a warrant to search for a document, parcel, or other thing in the custody of the postal authority.

**Why.** The power to issue a search-warrant for a document, parcel, or other thing in the custody of the postal authority is restricted to either a District Magistrate or a Chief Judicial Magistrate. No other Magistrate can exercise this power.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §96

items.q: What is the maximum number of persons that, if exceeded, constitutes a class of persons that can be used to establish the abetting of an offence?
items.ref: Ten or more

A1.t:
**Answer.** A group of six or more persons acting in concert constitutes a class of persons that can be used to establish the abetting of an offence.

**Why.** The law specifies that for an act to be considered as abetting through a class of persons, there must be at least six individuals involved in concert. This threshold ensures that the act of abetting is significant and involves a substantial group.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** If the number of persons exceeds ten, then the public generally or a number or class of persons can be considered for establishing the abetting of an offence.

**Why.** The statute specifically mentions that abetting an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten would be punishable. This indicates that the threshold for classifying a group as a class of persons for the purpose of abetting an offence is ten individuals.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §57

A3.t:
**Answer.** The abetment of an offence is established if it is done by any person who belongs to a class of five or more persons.

**Why.** The law requires that the abetment must be committed by a person who belongs to a class of five or more persons. This class membership is a necessary condition for the offense to be established.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §51

A4.t:
**Answer.** The abetment of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten is punishable.

**Why.** The law specifies that abetment of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten is punishable with imprisonment up to seven years and a fine. This establishes the threshold for the class of persons involved in the abetment.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §57

items.q: What is the maximum punishment that an offender can receive when they have committed multiple offences that are each punishable by a different punishment?
items.ref: The offender shall not be punished with the punishment of more than one of such his offences, unless it be so expressly provided.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum punishment that an offender can receive for multiple offences is the highest punishment among the offences committed.

**Why.** When an individual commits multiple offences, the court will impose the sentence for the most serious offence, unless the legislature has provided for cumulative punishments. In the absence of such provision, the principle of punishment for the most serious offence applies.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §105

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum punishment an offender can receive when they have committed multiple offences is the punishment for the offence with the highest penalty if the same punishment is not provided for all offences.

**Why.** This rule ensures that an offender is not punished more severely than the least severe punishment provided for any of the offences committed, thereby preventing cumulative punishments that exceed the least severe penalty.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §10

A3.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and also liable to a fine.

**Why.** When an offender has committed two or more offences, each of which is punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term exceeding seven years, the law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and also liable to a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §45

A4.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with the punishment of the offence for which the lowest punishment is provided, unless the same punishment is provided for all offences.

**Why.** The law dictates that if a person is found guilty of multiple offences, the punishment must be determined based on the lowest punishment provided for any of the offences. This rule applies even if the offender is found guilty of all the specified offences.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §10

items.q: What is the maximum term for which a Special Judicial Magistrate can be appointed?
items.ref: One year at a time, as directed by the High Court.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A Special Judicial Magistrate can be appointed for a term not exceeding five years.

**Why.** This term is set to ensure regular rotation of magistrates, thereby promoting judicial efficiency and minimizing potential biases over time.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term for which a Special Judicial Magistrate can be appointed is one year.

**Why.** The law specifies that a Special Judicial Magistrate can be appointed for a term not exceeding one year at a time, as directed by the High Court.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §11

A3.t:
**Answer.** The appointment of a Special Judicial Magistrate shall not exceed three years.

**Why.** The law stipulates that the appointment of a Special Judicial Magistrate shall not exceed a period of three years.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §15

A4.t:
**Answer.** A Special Judicial Magistrate can be appointed for a term not exceeding one year at a time.

**Why.** The appointment of a Special Judicial Magistrate is limited by a specific term. This term cannot exceed one year at a time, and the duration of the appointment is determined by the High Court through either a general or special order.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §11

items.q: What is the maximum term of imprisonment that an individual can be sentenced to for attempting to seduce a soldier from their duty?
items.ref: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years.

A1.t:
**Answer.** An individual attempting to seduce a soldier from their duty can be sentenced to a maximum term of imprisonment for three years.

**Why.** The statute aims to protect the integrity of military personnel and their duties. The maximum sentence reflects the seriousness of undermining military discipline and morale.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** An individual can be sentenced to imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years.

**Why.** The statute specifically outlines the penalties for abetting the committing of mutiny or attempting to seduce a soldier from their duty, which includes a maximum term of imprisonment of ten years.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §159

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend up to ten years.

**Why.** The law mandates that the punishment for this offense is imprisonment for a term extending up to ten years. This penalty applies regardless of whether the attempt was successful or not.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §154

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment is ten years.

**Why.** The law mandates that anyone who attempts to seduce a soldier from his allegiance or duty shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §159

items.q: What is the maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for fouling the water of a public spring or reservoir?
items.ref: The maximum term is six months.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for fouling the water of a public spring or reservoir is one year.

**Why.** Under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, fouling the water supply is considered a serious offense against public health and sanitation, and thus carries a moderate sentence to deter such actions.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §56

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for fouling the water of a public spring or reservoir is six months.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the punishment for such an offense includes imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, along with the possibility of a fine up to five thousand rupees, or both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §279

A3.t:
**Answer.** The offender may be punished with imprisonment up to one year.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to one year.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §275

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment is six months.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever voluntarily corrupts or fouls the water of any public spring or reservoir, rendering it less fit for its ordinary use, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §279

items.q: What is the maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for knowingly disobeying a quarantine rule?
items.ref: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for knowingly disobeying a quarantine rule is six months.

**Why.** Disobeying quarantine rules is considered a minor offense under public health regulations, and the statute sets a standard term of imprisonment to ensure compliance without imposing excessive penalties.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for knowingly disobeying a quarantine rule is six months.

**Why.** The statute specifically outlines the punishment for disobeying rules related to quarantining modes of transport, which includes a maximum term of six months' imprisonment.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §273

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment up to one year.

**Why.** The law mandates that any person who knowingly disobeys a quarantine rule shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §274

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment is six months.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever knowingly disobeys any rule related to quarantine faces a penalty of imprisonment up to six months, or a fine, or both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §273

items.q: What is the maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for neglecting to take measures to guard against probable danger to human life from the fall of a building?
items.ref: Six months

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for neglecting to take measures to guard against probable danger to human life from the fall of a building is one year.

**Why.** This provision aims to ensure public safety by penalizing those who fail to take necessary precautions against potential hazards. The relatively short term reflects the intent to deter such negligence without imposing overly harsh penalties.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** Six months.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the maximum term of imprisonment for neglecting to take measures to guard against probable danger to human life from the fall of a building is six months.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §290

A3.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment is three years.

**Why.** The law mandates that the person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §289

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment is six months.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever commits this offense shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §290

items.q: What is the maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for the offense of obstructing a public servant in the discharge of their public functions?
items.ref: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for the offense of obstructing a public servant in the discharge of their public functions is six months.

**Why.** This provision aims to deter interference with the lawful duties of public servants. It reflects the principle that such acts, while minor in nature, can disrupt public order and efficiency.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §154

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for the offense of obstructing a public servant in the discharge of their public functions is three months.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the punishment for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of their public functions includes imprisonment for a term that may extend to three months, along with the possibility of a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §221

A3.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years.

**Why.** The law mandates that the punishment for this offense is imprisonment of either description for a term extending up to two years.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §194

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment is three months.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever voluntarily obstructs any public servant in the discharge of his public functions shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §221

items.q: What is the maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by a class of persons exceeding ten?
items.ref: Seven years

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by a class of persons exceeding ten is ten years.

**Why.** The statute aims to deter widespread criminal activities by imposing significant penalties on those who encourage such offenses among large groups. This provision ensures that individuals who incite crimes affecting a broad segment of society face substantial consequences.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by a class of persons exceeding ten is seven years.

**Why.** The statute specifically provides for a term of imprisonment that may extend to seven years for such abetment.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §57

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years.

**Why.** If the abetment is directed at the public generally or at any class of persons exceeding ten, the punishment is imprisonment for a term extending up to seven years.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §51

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment is seven years.

**Why.** The law mandates that anyone who abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and with fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §57

items.q: What is the maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who causes evidence of an offence punishable with death to disappear, with the intention of screening the offender?
items.ref: Seven years.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed is ten years, along with a fine.

**Why.** This provision aims to deter the destruction of evidence that could lead to the conviction of a person guilty of a serious offense. The penalty reflects the seriousness of tampering with evidence intended to shield a person from justice.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §56

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed is seven years.

**Why.** The statute specifies that if the offence known or believed to have been committed is punishable with death, the person causing the evidence to disappear will be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §238(a)

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend up to ten years.

**Why.** The law mandates that anyone who intentionally causes evidence of an offence punishable with death to disappear shall be punished with imprisonment for a term extending up to ten years.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §241

A4.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that if the offence known or believed to have been committed is punishable with death, the offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §238

items.q: What is the maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who falsifies accounts or makes false entries in a book or electronic record?
items.ref: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who falsifies accounts or makes false entries in a book or electronic record is seven years.

**Why.** This provision aims to deter financial fraud and ensure accurate record-keeping. The penalty is designed to balance the severity of the offense with the need to maintain economic integrity and public trust in financial systems.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §215

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who falsifies accounts or makes false entries in a book or electronic record is seven years.

**Why.** This punishment is prescribed for individuals who, with the intent to defraud, destroy, alter, mutilate, or falsify any book, electronic record, paper, writing, valuable security, or account belonging to their employer, or for which they are responsible. The statute also covers cases where false entries are made or altered with the intent to defraud.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §344

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment for a term extending up to seven years. This punishment applies regardless of whether the act was done fraudulently or dishonestly.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §241

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment is seven years.

**Why.** The law specifies that whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall be used for the purpose of cheating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §344

items.q: What is the maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who fraudulently cancels or destroys a will or valuable security?
items.ref: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who fraudulently cancels or destroys a will or valuable security is seven years, along with a fine.

**Why.** The statute aims to deter fraudulent acts that can lead to disputes over property rights and financial interests. The prescribed term of imprisonment reflects the seriousness of such actions while allowing for a range of penalties depending on the circumstances of the case.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §245

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who fraudulently cancels or destroys a will or valuable security is seven years.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the punishment includes imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §343

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment for a term extending up to seven years. This punishment applies regardless of whether the act was done fraudulently or dishonestly.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §315

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment is seven years.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever fraudulently or dishonestly cancels, destroys, or defaces a document, or attempts to do so, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §343

items.q: What is the maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who gives false information to screen an offender who committed an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term not extending to ten years?
items.ref: One-fourth part of the longest term of the imprisonment provided for the offence.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed is six months.

**Why.** This penalty reflects the seriousness of providing false information to obstruct justice, but it is limited to a shorter term to balance the need for deterrence with proportionality.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed is one-fourth part of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both.

**Why.** This provision outlines the penalties for giving false information with the intent to screen an offender from legal punishment. The specific term of imprisonment depends on the severity of the original offense, and for offenses not punishable with ten years of imprisonment, the penalty is one-fourth of the longest term of imprisonment for that offense.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §238

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years.

**Why.** The law mandates that if the offence is punishable with imprisonment up to ten years, the punishment for giving false information is imprisonment for a term that may extend to two years.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §236

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment is one-fourth part of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both.

**Why.** The penalty structure for giving false information to screen an offender depends on the severity of the underlying offence. For offences punishable with imprisonment up to ten years, the punishment is imprisonment for a term up to one-fourth of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §238

items.q: What is the maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who voluntarily causes hurt to a public servant in the discharge of their duty?
items.ref: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who voluntarily causes hurt to a public servant in the discharge of their duty is three years.

**Why.** The statute aims to protect public servants who are performing their official duties and ensures that those who cause them harm face appropriate consequences without overly harsh penalties.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §254

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who voluntarily causes hurt to a public servant in the discharge of their duty is five years.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the punishment for voluntarily causing hurt to a public servant in the discharge of their duty includes imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §121

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend up to two years.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment for a term extending up to two years. This punishment applies regardless of whether the act was done with or without the intent to cause death or injury.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §145

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment is five years.

**Why.** The law specifies that whoever voluntarily causes hurt to a public servant while they are performing their duty faces a penalty of imprisonment up to five years, or a fine, or both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §121

items.q: What is the maximum term of imprisonment that may be imposed on a person who threatens another with intent to cause them to give false evidence?
items.ref: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that may be imposed on a person who threatens another with intent to cause them to give false evidence is three years, and the offender is also liable to a fine.

**Why.** The statute aims to deter the act of threatening to provide false evidence, which can undermine the integrity of judicial proceedings. The prescribed term reflects the seriousness of such an offense while providing a deterrent effect.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of imprisonment that may be imposed on a person who threatens another with intent to cause them to give false evidence is seven years.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the punishment for threatening another with injury to their person, reputation, or property with intent to cause false evidence includes imprisonment for a term that may extend to seven years, along with fine or both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §232

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment for a term extending up to seven years. This punishment applies regardless of whether the threat was made in writing or otherwise.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §234

A4.t:
**Answer.** The person may be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever threatens another with injury to their person, reputation, or property, or to the person or reputation of someone they are interested in, with the intent to cause them to give false evidence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §232

items.q: What is the maximum term of simple imprisonment that can be imposed for refusing to sign a statement when required to do so by a public servant?
items.ref: Three months

A1.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of simple imprisonment that can be imposed for refusing to sign a statement when required to do so by a public servant is six months.

**Why.** This provision limits the duration of imprisonment to ensure that the penalty is proportionate to the offense of non-compliance with a public servant's request for a statement.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §56

A2.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of simple imprisonment that can be imposed for refusing to sign a statement when required to do so by a public servant is three months.

**Why.** The statute specifies that refusal to sign a statement as required by a public servant results in a punishment with simple imprisonment for a term that may extend to three months, along with the possibility of a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §215

A3.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of simple imprisonment is six months.

**Why.** The law provides that if a person refuses to sign a statement when required to do so by a public servant, they shall be punished with simple imprisonment up to six months.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §236

A4.t:
**Answer.** The maximum term of simple imprisonment is three months.

**Why.** The punishment for refusing to sign a statement is simple imprisonment up to three months, or a fine up to three thousand rupees, or both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §215

items.q: What is the minimum age and mental state required for a person to become an agent?
items.ref: Not of the age of majority and not of sound mind.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A person must be of the age of majority and of sound mind to become an agent.

**Why.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, requires that an agent must be competent to contract, which includes being of the age of majority and of sound mind.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §11

A2.t:
**Answer.** A person must be of the age of majority and of sound mind to become an agent.

**Why.** The law stipulates that an individual must meet both criteria of being of the age of majority and being of sound mind to qualify as an agent. These conditions ensure that the person has the necessary legal capacity to enter into agreements and manage responsibilities on behalf of others.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §183

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person must be of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and they must be of sound mind.

**Why.** An agency can only be established if the person who is to act as an agent is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and if that person is also of sound mind.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §180

A4.t:
**Answer.** A person must be of the age of majority according to the law to which they are subject, and they must also be of sound mind.

**Why.** To become an agent, a person must meet two criteria: first, they must be of the age of majority according to the law to which they are subject; second, they must be of sound mind. These conditions define the basic competency required for agency.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §183

items.q: What is the minimum amount of fine that can be imposed for the intentional omission to give information respecting an offence?
items.ref: Up to five thousand rupees

A1.t:
**Answer.** The minimum amount of fine that can be imposed for the intentional omission to give information respecting an offence is Rs. 100.

**Why.** The statute sets out the minimum and maximum fines for various offenses, ensuring that there is a deterrent for individuals who intentionally fail to report crimes they are aware of.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §56

A2.t:
**Answer.** The minimum amount of fine that can be imposed for the intentional omission to give information respecting an offence is five thousand rupees.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the penalty for such an omission includes a fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, indicating that this is the minimum amount.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §239

A3.t:
**Answer.** The fine must be at least five thousand rupees.

**Why.** The law mandates that the fine imposed shall not be less than five thousand rupees. This minimum fine applies regardless of whether the omission was intentional or negligent.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §235

A4.t:
**Answer.** The minimum fine that can be imposed is five thousand rupees.

**Why.** The penalty structure for the offense requires the individual to face imprisonment or fine, or both. For the offense of omitting to give information, the minimum fine specified is five thousand rupees.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §239

items.q: What is the minimum distance from the prison at which the attendance of the person is required for giving evidence, making the officer not abstain from carrying out the Court's order?
items.ref: The minimum distance is 25 kilometres.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The minimum distance from the prison at which the person is required to attend for giving evidence is 50 kilometers, unless the court orders otherwise.

**Why.** This provision ensures that the inconvenience to the witness is minimized while still allowing the court to conduct its proceedings effectively. The court may order a shorter distance if it deems it necessary for the administration of justice.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §124

A2.t:
**Answer.** The minimum distance from the prison at which the attendance of the person is required for giving evidence, making the officer not abstain from carrying out the Court's order, is not more than twenty-five kilometres.

**Why.** The statute specifically states that the officer in charge of the prison shall not abstain from carrying out the Court's order if the attendance of such person is required for giving evidence at a place not more than twenty-five kilometres distance from the prison.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §304

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person must be brought to attend before the Court at a place that is not less than five miles from the prison.

**Why.** The law mandates that the person must be brought to attend before the Court at a place that is not less than five miles from the prison. This requirement ensures that the person is physically present in a location sufficiently distant from the prison.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §485

A4.t:
**Answer.** The attendance must be required for giving evidence at a place not more than twenty-five kilometres distance from the prison.

**Why.** The law specifies that the officer in charge of the prison shall not abstain from carrying out the Court's order if the attendance of the person is required for giving evidence at a place not more than twenty-five kilometres distance from the prison.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §304

items.q: What is the minimum duration of imprisonment for the intentional omission to give information respecting an offence?
items.ref: Up to six months

A1.t:
**Answer.** The minimum duration of imprisonment for the intentional omission to give information respecting an offence is six months.

**Why.** This penalty is designed to deter individuals from withholding information that could be crucial in the investigation and prosecution of crimes. The specific duration reflects the seriousness of the offense while providing a deterrent effect.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** The minimum duration of imprisonment for the intentional omission to give information respecting an offence is six months.

**Why.** This penalty applies when the omission relates to the commission of an offence, or is required for the purpose of preventing an offence, or in order to apprehend an offender. The statute specifically mandates a longer term of imprisonment compared to other offenses.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §239

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years.

**Why.** The law mandates that the person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years. This punishment applies when the omission is done intentionally or negligently.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §236

A4.t:
**Answer.** The minimum duration of imprisonment is one month.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever intentionally omits to give information respecting an offence, when legally bound to do so, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §239

items.q: What is the minimum duration of simple imprisonment that a public servant can receive for engaging in trade illegally?
items.ref: The minimum duration is one year.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A public servant can receive a minimum of six months of simple imprisonment for engaging in trade illegally.

**Why.** The statute aims to deter public servants from engaging in commercial activities, which could lead to conflicts of interest or misuse of power. The specified minimum term ensures a significant deterrent effect.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** One year

**Why.** The statute specifies that a public servant who engages in trade illegally will face simple imprisonment for a term that may extend to one year, along with possible fines or community service.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §202

A3.t:
**Answer.** The minimum term of imprisonment must be at least six months.

**Why.** The law mandates that the punishment includes imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months. This minimum term applies to the imprisonment component of the penalty.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §194

A4.t:
**Answer.** The minimum duration of simple imprisonment is one year.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever engages in trade while legally bound not to do so shall face simple imprisonment for a term extending up to one year, or a fine, or both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §202

items.q: What is the minimum information that must be communicated to an accused in a summons-case when they appear before the Magistrate?
items.ref: The particulars of the offence of which the accused is accused shall be stated to them.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The accused must be informed of the charge against them, their right to legal representation, and the right to remain silent.

**Why.** This ensures that the accused is aware of the nature of the accusation and their rights during the proceedings, upholding the principles of fair trial and due process.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** The accused must be informed of the particulars of the offence of which they are accused and asked whether they plead guilty or have any defence to make.

**Why.** This ensures that the accused is aware of the charges against them and can make an informed decision regarding their plea or defence.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §274

A3.t:
**Answer.** The Magistrate must inform the accused of the substance of the charge and the date and time fixed for the trial.

**Why.** When an accused appears before the Magistrate, the Magistrate must inform them of two things: first, the substance of the charge; and second, the date and time that has been fixed for the trial.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §219

A4.t:
**Answer.** The Magistrate must state the particulars of the offence of which the accused is accused and ask whether the accused pleads guilty or has any defence to make.

**Why.** The law mandates that when the accused appears or is brought before the Magistrate, the Magistrate must first state the particulars of the offence and then ask the accused if they plead guilty or have any defence to make. This process is mandatory for all summons-cases.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §274

items.q: What is the minimum level of evidence required for a Court to take cognizance of an offence punishable under section 67 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, when the persons involved are in a marital relationship?
items.ref: Prima facie satisfaction of the facts that constitute the offence.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The Court requires prima facie evidence to take cognizance of an offence under section 67 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, when the persons involved are in a marital relationship.

**Why.** This requirement ensures that the Court only proceeds with cases where there is sufficient initial evidence to suggest the commission of an offense, thereby maintaining judicial discretion and ensuring that resources are not wasted on unfounded claims.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** The Court must have prima facie satisfaction of the facts constituting the offence upon a complaint filed or made by the wife against the husband.

**Why.** This requirement ensures that the Court only takes cognizance of such offences when there is a credible basis for the allegations, and it specifically protects marital relationships by requiring a complaint from the wife.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §221

A3.t:
**Answer.** The Court must be satisfied that there is reasonable ground to believe that the offence has been committed.

**Why.** For offences committed by persons in a marital relationship, the Court must be satisfied that there is reasonable ground to believe that the offence has been committed before taking cognizance.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §218

A4.t:
**Answer.** The Court must be satisfied that the facts constituting the offence have been established through a complaint filed by the wife against the husband.

**Why.** The law mandates that no Court can take cognizance of an offence under section 67 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, if the persons are in a marital relationship, unless the complaint is filed by the wife against the husband and the Court is satisfied that the facts constituting the offence are proven.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §221

items.q: What is the minimum level of sentence complexity that a court can direct in cases where an offender is punishable with imprisonment?
items.ref: The court can direct that the imprisonment be partly rigorous and the rest simple.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A court can direct a minimum sentence of six months' imprisonment.

**Why.** This ensures that even minor breaches of the law result in a tangible penalty, thereby upholding the seriousness of the legal system. The exact duration of six months is specified to provide a clear and consistent starting point for sentencing.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §56

A2.t:
**Answer.** In cases where an offender is punishable with imprisonment which may be of either description, the court can direct that such imprisonment shall be wholly rigorous, wholly simple, or any part of such imprisonment shall be rigorous and the rest simple.

**Why.** This provision allows for flexibility in sentencing, ensuring that the court can tailor the sentence to fit the specific circumstances of the case, thereby promoting just outcomes.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §7

A3.t:
**Answer.** The court must direct that the offender be sentenced to imprisonment for a term not less than one-fourth part of the longest term provided for the offence.

**Why.** When an offender is punishable with imprisonment, the court must direct that the offender shall be sentenced to imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one-fourth part of the longest term provided for the offence.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §451

A4.t:
**Answer.** The court must direct whether the imprisonment shall be wholly rigorous, wholly simple, or partially rigorous and partially simple.

**Why.** The law mandates that in every case where an offender is punishable with imprisonment, the court must direct the nature of the sentence. This direction must specify whether the imprisonment is wholly rigorous, wholly simple, or a combination of both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §7

items.q: What is the minimum punishment for a first-time offender who commits the offence of stalking?
items.ref: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The minimum punishment for a first-time offender who commits the offence of stalking is six months of rigorous imprisonment.

**Why.** The law aims to deter such behavior by imposing a significant but not overly harsh penalty for first-time offenders. This ensures that the punishment fits the crime while also providing an opportunity for rehabilitation.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** The minimum punishment for a first-time offender who commits the offence of stalking is imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the punishment for stalking includes imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and a fine. This applies to the first conviction of the offence.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §78

A3.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to a fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender must face imprisonment for a term extending up to three years. Additionally, the offender is also required to pay a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §139

A4.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever commits the offence of stalking shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §78

items.q: What is the minimum punishment that can be imposed on someone who attempts to cancel or destroy a will or valuable security with intent to cause damage or injury to the public or to any person?
items.ref: Imprisonment for life.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The minimum punishment that can be imposed on someone who attempts to cancel or destroy a will or valuable security with intent to cause damage or injury to the public or to any person is six months' imprisonment and a fine.

**Why.** The law aims to deter such actions by imposing a minimum sentence that reflects the seriousness of tampering with legal documents that could lead to significant financial or emotional harm.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §254

A2.t:
**Answer.** The minimum punishment that can be imposed is imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Why.** The statute specifies that the punishment for attempting to cancel, destroy, or deface a will or valuable security with intent to cause damage or injury includes imprisonment for a term that may extend to seven years and a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §343

A3.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment for a term extending up to ten years, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §154

A4.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever commits the offense faces imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term extending up to seven years, and liability to fine. This punishment applies regardless of whether the act was completed or merely attempted.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §343

items.q: What is the minimum punishment that can be imposed on someone who destroys or damages a place of worship with the intention of insulting a particular religion?
items.ref: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The minimum punishment that can be imposed is six months of imprisonment and a fine of at least 1,000 Indian Rupees.

**Why.** This minimum sentence is designed to deter acts of desecration and protect religious sentiments. It applies specifically to cases where the destruction or damage is done with the intent to insult a particular religion.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §254

A2.t:
**Answer.** Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years.

**Why.** The statute specifically outlines that destroying or damaging a place of worship with the intent to insult a particular religion is a criminal act, and the minimum punishment for such an offense is imprisonment for a term extending up to two years.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §298

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and they must also be liable to a fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment for a term extending up to three years, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §291

A4.t:
