**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever commits the act of destroying, damaging, or defiling a place of worship must face a penalty that includes imprisonment up to two years, or a fine, or both. This punishment applies when the act is done with the specific intent of insulting the religion of any class of persons.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §298

items.q: What is the minimum punishment that can be imposed on someone who knowingly aids or assists a State prisoner or prisoner of war in escaping from lawful custody?
items.ref: imprisonment for life or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years

A1.t:
**Answer.** The minimum punishment that can be imposed on someone who knowingly aids or assists a State prisoner or prisoner of war in escaping from lawful custody is six months of imprisonment.

**Why.** The law aims to deter any form of assistance to escapees to maintain the integrity of custodial systems. The specified minimum sentence ensures that even minor cases of aiding an escape are appropriately penalized.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §95

A2.t:
**Answer.** Imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Why.** The statute specifies that aiding or assisting a State prisoner or prisoner of war in escaping from lawful custody is a serious offense and mandates a severe punishment to deter such actions.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §158

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to a fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment for a term extending up to ten years, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §154

A4.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever knowingly aids or assists a State prisoner or prisoner of war in escaping from lawful custody shall face a minimum punishment of imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term up to ten years, along with liability to fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §158

items.q: What is the minimum punishment that must be imposed for the offense of obstructing a public servant in the discharge of their public functions?
items.ref: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The minimum punishment that must be imposed for the offense of obstructing a public servant in the discharge of their public functions is six months of imprisonment.

**Why.** This minimum sentence is mandated to ensure that individuals who obstruct public servants face a significant deterrent, thereby upholding the authority and efficiency of public service operations.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §154

A2.t:
**Answer.** Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months.

**Why.** The statute mandates a minimum sentence for obstructing a public servant, which includes imprisonment for a term that can extend up to three months.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §221

A3.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §194

A4.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand and five hundred rupees, or with both.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever voluntarily obstructs any public servant in the discharge of his public functions shall face a penalty involving imprisonment up to three months, or a fine up to two thousand and five hundred rupees, or both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §221

items.q: What is the minimum rank of Magistrate required to take cognizance of an offence, subject to the provisions of this Chapter?
items.ref: A Magistrate of the first class

A1.t:
**Answer.** A Magistrate of the first class is required to take cognizance of an offence, subject to the provisions of this Chapter.

**Why.** The minimum rank of Magistrate necessary to handle criminal cases is set to ensure adequate judicial oversight and expertise. This rule ensures that more serious cases are handled by magistrates who possess the necessary experience and authority.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** A Magistrate of the first class or a Magistrate of the second class specially empowered under sub-section (2) can take cognizance of an offence.

**Why.** The law specifies that cognizance can be taken by a Magistrate of the first class or, if specifically empowered, a Magistrate of the second class. This ensures that there are multiple levels of authority to handle complaints and reports of offences.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §210

A3.t:
**Answer.** The Magistrate must be a Judicial Magistrate.

**Why.** The power to take cognizance of an offence is restricted to a Judicial Magistrate. This requirement applies unless the provisions of this Chapter provide otherwise.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §218

A4.t:
**Answer.** Any Magistrate of the first class, or any Magistrate of the second class specially empowered in this behalf under sub-section (2), may take cognizance of any offence.

**Why.** The power to take cognizance is granted to any Magistrate of the first class, or any Magistrate of the second class who has been specially empowered under sub-section (2). This power is subject to the provisions of this Chapter.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §210

items.q: What is the minimum rank of a police officer that must be designated to maintain information about persons arrested, charges, and offences in every district and police station?
items.ref: A police officer not below the rank of Assistant Sub-Inspector of Police.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The minimum rank of a police officer designated to maintain information about persons arrested, charges, and offences in every district and police station is a Sub-Inspector.

**Why.** This ensures that there is a standardized level of responsibility and accountability for maintaining accurate records of arrests, charges, and offences within each district and police station, thereby improving transparency and efficiency in law enforcement.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** The minimum rank of a police officer that must be designated to maintain information about persons arrested, charges, and offences in every district and police station is Assistant Sub-Inspector of Police.

**Why.** According to the statute, the State Government is required to designate a police officer not below the rank of Assistant Sub-Inspector of Police for this responsibility.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §37

A3.t:
**Answer.** The officer must be at least an Inspector.

**Why.** The law mandates that the officer responsible for maintaining records must be at least an Inspector. This ensures that the person in charge has sufficient authority and experience to manage such sensitive information.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §59

A4.t:
**Answer.** The designated police officer must be not below the rank of Assistant Sub-Inspector of Police.

**Why.** The State Government must designate a police officer in every district and every police station, and this officer must be not below the rank of Assistant Sub-Inspector of Police. This officer is responsible for maintaining the information about the names and addresses of persons arrested, the nature of the offence charged, and ensuring this information is prominently displayed.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §37

items.q: What is the minimum requirement for a police officer to take a person arrested without warrant before?
items.ref: a Magistrate having jurisdiction in the case, or before the officer in charge of a police station.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A police officer must take a person arrested without a warrant before a magistrate without unnecessary delay.

**Why.** This ensures that the rights of the accused are protected and that the judicial process is initiated promptly to determine the validity of the arrest.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** A police officer making an arrest without warrant shall take or send the person arrested before a Magistrate having jurisdiction in the case, or before the officer in charge of a police station.

**Why.** This ensures that the arrested individual is brought before a judicial authority to determine the validity of the arrest and to decide on further proceedings, thereby safeguarding the rights of the arrested person.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §57

A3.t:
**Answer.** The officer must be a police officer in charge of a police station.

**Why.** The law requires that the person taken before must be taken before a police officer who is the police officer in charge of a police station.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §58

A4.t:
**Answer.** A police officer must take or send the person arrested before a Magistrate having jurisdiction in the case, or before the officer in charge of a police station, without unnecessary delay and subject to the provisions concerning bail.

**Why.** The law mandates that every police officer making an arrest without warrant must take or send the person arrested before a Magistrate or the officer in charge of a police station. This action must occur without unnecessary delay and must adhere to the provisions governing bail.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §57

items.q: What is the minimum requirement for a warrant of arrest issued by a Court under this Sanhita?
items.ref: The warrant must be in writing and signed by the presiding officer of the Court.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A warrant of arrest must be issued by a competent judicial authority.

**Why.** This ensures that any arrest made pursuant to a warrant is lawful and based on a proper judicial decision. The warrant must detail the grounds for the arrest and the identity of the accused to ensure due process is followed.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** A warrant of arrest issued by a Court under this Sanhita must be in writing, signed by the presiding officer of such Court and shall bear the seal of the Court.

**Why.** This ensures that the warrant is officially recognized and authenticated, providing a clear record of the authorization for the arrest and safeguarding against unauthorized actions.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §72

A3.t:
**Answer.** The warrant must be issued in duplicate.

**Why.** A warrant of arrest issued by a Court under this Sanhita shall be in duplicate.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §74

A4.t:
**Answer.** A warrant of arrest must be in writing, signed by the presiding officer of the Court, and must bear the seal of the Court.

**Why.** The law mandates that every warrant of arrest issued by a Court under this Sanhita must meet three criteria: it must be in writing, it must be signed by the presiding officer, and it must bear the seal of the Court.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §72

items.q: What is the minimum term of imprisonment for a public servant who fails to apprehend a person under sentence of a Court and the person is subject to imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term of ten years or upwards?
items.ref: Seven years.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A public servant who fails to apprehend a person under sentence of a Court and the person is subject to imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term of ten years or upwards is liable to a minimum term of imprisonment for six months.

**Why.** The statute aims to ensure that public servants fulfill their duties in apprehending individuals as ordered by courts, thereby upholding the rule of law. The specific term of six months is set to balance accountability with proportionality.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** With or without fine, the public servant shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to fourteen years.

**Why.** The statute specifies that if a public servant fails to apprehend a person under sentence of a Court and the person is subject to imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term of ten years or upwards, the penalty includes a term of imprisonment that can extend up to fourteen years, along with the option of a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §260(a)

A3.t:
**Answer.** The public servant shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years.

**Why.** If a public servant fails to apprehend a person under sentence of a Court and that person is liable to imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term of ten years or upwards, the punishment is imprisonment for a term extending up to seven years.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §195

A4.t:
**Answer.** The punishment is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, with or without fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that if a public servant legally bound to apprehend or confine a person under sentence of a Court is legally bound to apprehend or confine a person subject to imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term of ten years or upwards, the penalty is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, with or without fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §260

items.q: What is the minimum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for dishonest misappropriation of property?
items.ref: imprisonment of at least six months

A1.t:
**Answer.** The minimum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for dishonest misappropriation of property is six months.

**Why.** The statute aims to provide a deterrent against minor cases of dishonest misappropriation while ensuring that the punishment fits the crime. The minimum term ensures that even small-scale offenses are not overlooked but are appropriately addressed.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** The minimum term of imprisonment that can be imposed for dishonest misappropriation of property is one year.

**Why.** The statute specifies the range of punishments for various offenses, including dishonest misappropriation of property, which carries a minimum term of imprisonment of one year.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §315

A3.t:
**Answer.** The minimum term of imprisonment that may be imposed is six months.

**Why.** The law mandates that the punishment must include imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months. This minimum term applies to the offense of dishonestly misappropriating or converting property belonging to another person.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §315

A4.t:
**Answer.** The minimum term of imprisonment is three years.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever commits the offense shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §315

items.q: What is the minimum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who gives false information to screen an offender who committed an offence punishable with imprisonment for life?
items.ref: Three years.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The minimum term of imprisonment that can be imposed is six months.

**Why.** To deter the practice of giving false information to screen an offender, the law mandates a minimum sentence to ensure that such actions are discouraged and appropriately penalized.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** The minimum term of imprisonment that can be imposed is one year.

**Why.** The statute specifies that if the offence for which the offender is screened is punishable with imprisonment for life, the person giving false information can be imprisoned for a term which may extend to three years. Since the minimum term for such an offence is one year, the minimum term of imprisonment that can be imposed is one year.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §238

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years.

**Why.** The law mandates that anyone who gives false information to screen an offender shall be punished with imprisonment for a term extending up to ten years. This punishment applies regardless of whether the underlying offence was committed before or after the commencement of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §241

A4.t:
**Answer.** The minimum term of imprisonment is three years.

**Why.** The law mandates that anyone who gives false information to screen an offender faces a minimum imprisonment term of three years. This applies when the underlying offence is punishable with imprisonment for life.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §238

items.q: What is the minimum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who voluntarily causes grievous hurt to a public servant in the discharge of their duty?
items.ref: Imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The minimum term of imprisonment that can be imposed is six months.

**Why.** The law aims to deter such actions against public servants who are performing their duties. This minimum sentence ensures that individuals understand the seriousness of interfering with the lawful functions of public officials.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §254

A2.t:
**Answer.** The minimum term of imprisonment that can be imposed on someone who voluntarily causes grievous hurt to a public servant in the discharge of their duty is one year.

**Why.** The statute specifies that such an act is punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than one year and may extend up to ten years, along with a potential fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §121

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender must face imprisonment for a term extending up to ten years. This punishment applies regardless of whether the act was done with or without the intent to cause death.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §145

A4.t:
**Answer.** The minimum term of imprisonment must be at least one year, but it may extend up to ten years.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt to a public servant in the discharge of their duty faces a minimum imprisonment term of one year. This minimum term is subject to a maximum extension of ten years.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §121

items.q: What is the minimum value of property that can be sold by a Magistrate without the need to apply the provisions of sections 503 and 504?
items.ref: Less than ten thousand rupees.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The minimum value of property that can be sold by a Magistrate without applying the provisions of sections 503 and 504 is Rs. 10,000.

**Why.** This threshold ensures that minor transactions do not require the complex procedures outlined in sections 503 and 504, thereby streamlining the process for smaller sales.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §125

A2.t:
**Answer.** The minimum value of property that can be sold by a Magistrate without applying the provisions of sections 503 and 504 is five hundred rupees.

**Why.** This threshold is specified in the context of property that is subject to speedy and natural decay, where the person entitled to the possession of the property is unknown or absent, and the property's value is less than five hundred rupees, allowing for immediate sale by auction.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §106

A3.t:
**Answer.** The Magistrate may sell any property of a value not exceeding five thousand rupees.

**Why.** A Magistrate may sell any property of a value not exceeding five thousand rupees. This sale must be made in accordance with the provisions of section 502.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §501

A4.t:
**Answer.** Property whose value is less than five hundred rupees can be sold by a Magistrate without applying the provisions of sections 503 and 504.

**Why.** The law allows a Magistrate to sell property whose value is less than five hundred rupees without applying the provisions of sections 503 and 504. This provision applies when the person entitled to the property is unknown or absent, and the property is subject to speedy and natural decay.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §505

items.q: What is the nature of the infectious disease that can be prevalent in a place, leading to regulation of intercourse with other places?
items.ref: An infectious disease.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The nature of the infectious disease that can lead to such regulation is one that poses a significant risk to public health and safety.

**Why.** Regulations are put in place to prevent the spread of serious infectious diseases that could endanger the general population. The specific disease must be identified as posing a substantial threat before any restrictions on inter-state or inter-district movement are imposed.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** The nature of the infectious disease that can be prevalent in a place, leading to regulation of intercourse with other places, is not specified in the provided provisions.

**Why.** The provisions focus on the actions related to spreading or preventing the spread of infectious diseases but do not specify the exact nature or type of infectious disease that can trigger such regulations.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §271

A3.t:
**Answer.** The disease must be one that is dangerous to life and is not yet known to be transmissible from person to person.

**Why.** The regulation applies when an infectious disease is present in a place. This disease must be dangerous to life and must not be known to be transmissible from person to person.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §195

A4.t:
**Answer.** The infectious disease must be dangerous to life.

**Why.** The law addresses the regulation of intercourse when an infectious disease is present. This regulation applies specifically to diseases that are dangerous to life.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §273

items.q: What is the obligation of the party who rescinds the contract if they have received a benefit from the other party?
items.ref: The party rescinding avoidable contract shall, if he have received any benefit thereunder from another party to such contract, restore such benefit, so far as may be, to the person from whom it was received.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The party who rescinds the contract must restore to the other party any benefit received under the contract or return any consideration paid by the other party.

**Why.** When a contract is rescinded, the parties are restored to their positions before the contract was made. This includes returning any benefits received or payments made under the contract.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §65

A2.t:
**Answer.** The party who rescinds the contract must restore any benefit received from the other party, to the extent possible.

**Why.** When a contract is rescinded, the party who initiated the rescission is under a duty to return any benefits conferred upon them by the other party. This ensures that the contract is effectively nullified without causing undue financial loss to either party.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §64

A3.t:
**Answer.** The party who rescinds must make compensation to the other party for any benefit that was received.

**Why.** If a party rescinds a contract and has received a benefit, they are required to make compensation to the other party for that benefit.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §59

A4.t:
**Answer.** The party who rescinds the contract must restore the benefit they received, or make compensation for it, to the person from whom they received it.

**Why.** If a person at whose option a contract is voidable rescinds it, they are required to restore any benefit they received from the other party. This restoration or compensation applies even if the contract is subsequently found to be void.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §64

items.q: What is the officer in charge of the prison required to do with the prisoner while they are in custody in or near the Court?
items.ref: To keep the prisoner in custody until examined or authorized to return to the prison.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The officer in charge of the prison is required to produce the prisoner before the court at any time it may require.

**Why.** This ensures that the court can exercise its authority over the prisoner and manage the proceedings effectively. The officer must comply with the court's orders regarding the prisoner's appearance and treatment during the trial.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §154

A2.t:
**Answer.** The officer in charge of the prison shall cause the person named in the order to be taken to the Court in which his attendance is required, so as to be present there at the time mentioned in the order, and shall cause him to be kept in custody in or near the Court until he has been examined or until the Court authorises him to be taken back to the prison in which he was confined or detained.

**Why.** This requirement ensures that the prisoner appears before the Court as ordered and remains under the control of the prison authorities during the examination or hearing, maintaining security and order in the judicial process.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §305

A3.t:
**Answer.** The officer must take reasonable care of the prisoner and ensure that the prisoner is not exposed to any risk of injury.

**Why.** The officer in charge of the prison must take reasonable care of the prisoner and must also ensure that the prisoner is not exposed to any risk of injury.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §518

A4.t:
**Answer.** The officer in charge must keep the person in custody in or near the Court until the person has been examined or until the Court authorizes the person to be taken back to the prison.

**Why.** The officer in charge of the prison must keep the person in custody in or near the Court until the person has been examined or until the Court authorizes the person to be taken back to the prison.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §305

items.q: What is the outcome if the Magistrate considers the accusation as groundless, and what effect does this have on the accused?
items.ref: The accused shall be released and such release shall have the effect of discharge.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The Magistrate shall dismiss the complaint if it is found to be groundless.

**Why.** When an accusation lacks merit, the judicial process aims to ensure that resources are not wasted on unfounded claims, thereby protecting the rights and reputation of the accused.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** If the Magistrate considers the accusation as groundless, he shall, after recording reasons in writing, release the accused and such release shall have the effect of discharge.

**Why.** According to the statute, when the Magistrate determines that the accusation lacks merit, he must document his reasoning and then release the accused, effectively ending the legal proceedings against them.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §274

A3.t:
**Answer.** If the Magistrate finds no ground for the accusation, he shall dismiss it without inquiring into or trying the matter.

**Why.** The Magistrate has the power to dismiss the case if he determines that there is no ground for the accusation. This dismissal occurs before any inquiry or trial takes place.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §219

A4.t:
**Answer.** If the Magistrate considers the accusation as groundless, he must record reasons in writing and release the accused. This release has the effect of discharge.

**Why.** The law mandates that if the Magistrate determines the accusation is groundless, he must record reasons in writing and release the accused. This release explicitly has the effect of discharge.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §274

items.q: What is the outcome when a complainant is allowed to withdraw their complaint against an accused?
items.ref: The accused is acquitted.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The complaint is dismissed, and the proceedings are terminated.

**Why.** Once a complainant decides to withdraw their complaint, the court respects this decision, ensuring that the accused is not unnecessarily subjected to further legal processes.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** The accused against whom the complaint is withdrawn will be acquitted.

**Why.** When a complainant satisfies the Magistrate that there are sufficient grounds for withdrawing the complaint, the Magistrate may permit the withdrawal. Upon such withdrawal, the accused is acquitted unless the conviction is later set aside.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §280

A3.t:
**Answer.** The withdrawal of the complaint results in the discharge of the accused.

**Why.** If the complainant is allowed to withdraw the complaint, the accused shall be discharged.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §249

A4.t:
**Answer.** If the Magistrate permits the complainant to withdraw the complaint, the accused is automatically acquitted.

**Why.** The law provides that if a complainant satisfies the Magistrate that there are sufficient grounds for withdrawing the complaint, the Magistrate may permit the withdrawal. This action results in the accused being acquitted.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §280

items.q: What is the outcome when a suit under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, results in the obtaining of relief or compensation?
items.ref: The relief or compensation shall be dealt with according to the respective interests of the bailor and the bailee.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The court may grant the relief or compensation sought by the plaintiff.

**Why.** When a contract is valid and enforceable, the court will provide the appropriate relief or compensation as requested by the party who has suffered a breach of the contract.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §74

A2.t:
**Answer.** The party who suffered loss due to the breach of contract is entitled to receive compensation from the party who broke the contract.

**Why.** When a contract is breached, the law mandates that the aggrieved party should be compensated for any loss or damage that naturally arises from the breach, provided the damage was foreseeable at the time the contract was made. This compensation is intended to put the aggrieved party in the position they would have been in had the contract been fulfilled.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §73

A3.t:
**Answer.** The Court may direct that the amount of the compensation or relief be paid to the person who obtained it.

**Why.** If a suit under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, results in the obtaining of relief or compensation, the Court has the power to direct that the amount of such compensation or relief be paid to the person who obtained it.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §459

A4.t:
**Answer.** The Court may direct that the amount of the compensation or damages awarded be paid out of the funds of the person who obtained the relief or compensation.

**Why.** If a person obtains relief or compensation through a suit under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, the Court has the power to direct that the amount of the compensation or damages awarded be paid out of the funds of that person.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §449

items.q: What is the penalty for attempting to seduce any officer, soldier, sailor, or airman from their allegiance or duty in the Indian Armed Forces?
items.ref: Imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

A1.t:
**Answer.** Attempting to seduce any officer, soldier, sailor, or airman from their allegiance or duty in the Indian Armed Forces is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may be extended to seven years and shall also be liable to a fine.

**Why.** The statute aims to protect the integrity and discipline of the armed forces by penalizing actions that could undermine their cohesion and loyalty. The specific term and fine reflect the serious nature of such an attempt.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §95

A2.t:
**Answer.** Whoever attempts to seduce any officer, soldier, sailor, or airman from their allegiance or duty in the Indian Armed Forces will be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Why.** The law imposes severe penalties to deter actions that could undermine the loyalty and discipline of military personnel, ensuring the stability and effectiveness of the armed forces.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §159

A3.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that anyone who attempts to seduce an officer, soldier, sailor, or airman from their allegiance or duty shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years, along with a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §154

A4.t:
**Answer.** The punishment is imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term extending up to ten years, and the offender is also liable to fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever abets the committing of mutiny by an officer, soldier, sailor, or airman, or attempts to seduce them from their allegiance or duty, shall face imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to ten years, along with liability to fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §159

items.q: What is the penalty that a person is liable to if they fail to comply with an order under section 154?
items.ref: The person is liable to the penalty specified in section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A person who fails to comply with an order under section 154 is liable to a fine not exceeding one thousand rupees.

**Why.** Section 154 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, empowers the metropolitan magistrate to issue orders for the production of documents or the attendance of witnesses. Non-compliance with such an order can result in a financial penalty to enforce the order.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §154

A2.t:
**Answer.** The person is liable to the penalty specified in section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and the order shall be made absolute.

**Why.** According to the statute, if a person against whom an order is made under section 154 does not perform the required act or appear and show cause, they will face the penalty as specified in section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and the order will be made absolute.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §155

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with a fine, or with both.

**Why.** If a person fails to comply with an order made under section 154, they are liable to punishment with imprisonment of either description for a term extending up to six months, or with a fine, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §156

A4.t:
**Answer.** The person is liable to the penalty specified in section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

**Why.** If the person against whom an order is made under section 154 does not perform the act or appear and show cause, they are liable to the penalty specified in section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and the order shall be made absolute.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §155

items.q: What is the penalty that a person will be liable to in case of disobedience of the order?
items.ref: The penalty provided by section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A person who disobeys an order may be punished with a simple imprisonment for a term which may be six months or with a fine or with both.

**Why.** Disobedience to an order issued under certain provisions of the law is considered a contempt of court and is subject to penalties to ensure compliance with judicial authority.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §95

A2.t:
**Answer.** The person will be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand and five hundred rupees, or with both.

**Why.** Disobedience of an order by a public servant, especially when it causes or tends to cause obstruction, annoyance, or injury, is considered a criminal offense under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §223. The penalty varies depending on the severity of the consequences resulting from the disobedience.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §223

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with a fine, or with both.

**Why.** Disobedience of the order results in punishment with imprisonment up to six months, or with a fine, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §169

A4.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand and five hundred rupees, or with both.

**Why.** The penalty structure for disobedience is defined by the degree of harm caused. If the disobedience causes or tends to cause obstruction, annoyance, or injury, the penalty is simple imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to two thousand five hundred rupees, or both. If the disobedience causes or tends to cause danger to human life, health, or safety, or a riot or affray, the penalty is imprisonment up to one year, or a fine up to five thousand rupees, or both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §223

items.q: What is the presumption established by the Court regarding electronic or digital records?
items.ref: The Court shall presume the genuineness of every electronic or digital record...

A1.t:
**Answer.** The Court shall presume the authenticity of electronic or digital records if they are in a format commonly used at the time the record was made.

**Why.** This presumption is designed to facilitate the admissibility of electronic evidence in courts while acknowledging the modern nature of digital communication and records.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** The Court shall presume the genuineness of every electronic or digital record purporting to be the Official Gazette or purporting to be an electronic or digital record directed by any law to be kept by any person.

**Why.** This presumption applies when the record is kept in the form required by law and is produced from proper custody. Proper custody is defined as the place where the document is required to be kept and looked after by the designated person, or if the origin of the record is legitimate and the circumstances suggest its legitimacy.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §81

A3.t:
**Answer.** The Court shall presume that an electronic record was made by the person who purports to have made it.

**Why.** The law establishes a presumption that any electronic record was made by the person who claims to have made it. This presumption applies when the record is produced in court and no contrary evidence is presented.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §84

A4.t:
**Answer.** The Court shall presume the genuineness of every electronic or digital record purporting to be the Official Gazette, or purporting to be an electronic or digital record directed by any law to be kept by any person, provided the record is kept substantially in the form required by law and is produced from proper custody.

**Why.** The Court shall presume the genuineness of every electronic or digital record purporting to be the Official Gazette, or purporting to be an electronic or digital record directed by any law to be kept by any person, if such electronic or digital record is kept substantially in the form required by law and is produced from proper custody.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §81

items.q: What is the primary authority responsible for controlling the Chief Judicial Magistrate's definition of local limits?
items.ref: The High Court

A1.t:
**Answer.** The High Court is the primary authority responsible for controlling the Chief Judicial Magistrate's definition of local limits.

**Why.** The High Court has the jurisdiction to review and control the orders made by lower courts, including the definition of local limits by a Chief Judicial Magistrate, to ensure they are in accordance with the law.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §154

A2.t:
**Answer.** The High Court controls the Chief Judicial Magistrate's definition of local limits.

**Why.** The High Court has the authority to oversee and control how the Chief Judicial Magistrate defines the local limits of the areas where magistrates can exercise their powers.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §12

A3.t:
**Answer.** The High Court has the authority to define and alter the local limits of the Chief Judicial Magistrate.

**Why.** The power to define and alter the local limits of the Chief Judicial Magistrate rests with the High Court. This authority allows the High Court to establish or modify these boundaries as necessary.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §15

A4.t:
**Answer.** The High Court controls the Chief Judicial Magistrate's power to define local limits.

**Why.** The power to define local limits for the Chief Judicial Magistrate is controlled by the High Court. This control applies when the Chief Judicial Magistrate defines the local limits for the Magistrates appointed under sections 9 or 11.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §12

items.q: What is the primary characteristic of a leading question?
items.ref: A leading question suggests the answer the person putting it wishes or expects to receive.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A leading question suggests the answer or contains a statement of fact assumed to be true.

**Why.** Leading questions are prohibited during cross-examination to ensure that the witness is giving their own testimony rather than repeating what they have been told. This helps maintain the integrity of the judicial process.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §125

A2.t:
**Answer.** A leading question suggests the answer the questioner desires or expects.

**Why.** Leading questions are characterized by their tendency to guide the respondent towards a specific answer, often making it easier for the questioner to influence the response.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §146

A3.t:
**Answer.** A leading question is one that suggests the answer to the question.

**Why.** The definition of a leading question is that it is a question that suggests the answer to the question.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §149

A4.t:
**Answer.** A leading question is defined as one that suggests the answer the person asking it desires or expects to receive.

**Why.** A leading question is characterized by its purpose of suggesting the answer the person asking it desires or expects to receive. This definition establishes the core nature of the question type.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §146

items.q: What is the primary consideration in fixing the amount of a bond executed under this Chapter?
items.ref: The amount of every bond is fixed with due regard to the circumstances of the case.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The primary consideration in fixing the amount of a bond is the nature and gravity of the offense.

**Why.** The bond amount is intended to ensure that the accused appears in court and does not interfere with the administration of justice. The amount is set based on the seriousness of the offense to balance the interests of the public and the individual.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** The amount of every bond executed under this Chapter shall be fixed with due regard to the circumstances of the case and shall not be excessive.

**Why.** The law emphasizes that the bond amount must be reasonable and proportionate to the circumstances, ensuring that it is neither too high nor too low, thus preventing undue financial burden on the individual.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §484

A3.t:
**Answer.** The amount of the bond must be fixed based on the nature and gravity of the offense committed.

**Why.** The amount of the bond is determined by the nature and gravity of the offense that was committed. This ensures that the financial burden is proportionate to the severity of the crime.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §495

A4.t:
**Answer.** The amount of every bond must be fixed with due regard to the circumstances of the case and must not be excessive.

**Why.** The law mandates that the amount of every bond executed under this Chapter must be fixed with due regard to the circumstances of the case and must not be excessive. Furthermore, the High Court or the Court of Session may direct that the bail required by a police officer or Magistrate be reduced.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §484

items.q: What is the primary distinguishing factor between express and implied authority under the Indian Contract Act, 1872?
items.ref: Express authority is given by words spoken or written, while implied authority is inferred from circumstances of the case.

A1.t:
**Answer.** Express authority is stated directly in writing, while implied authority is inferred from the conduct of the parties or the nature of the business.

**Why.** Express authority is clearly defined and documented, whereas implied authority arises when the principal's conduct or the nature of the business leads to an understanding that certain actions can be taken without explicit permission.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §10

A2.t:
**Answer.** Express authority is given by words spoken or written, while implied authority can be inferred from the circumstances of the case.

**Why.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, distinguishes between express and implied authority based on how the authority is communicated. Express authority is clearly stated, whereas implied authority arises from the context and dealings between the parties.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §187

A3.t:
**Answer.** Express authority is given when the person in charge of the business explicitly authorizes the agent to perform certain acts. Implied authority arises when the person in charge of the business does not explicitly authorize the agent but allows the agent to do something that is necessary for the purpose of the agency.

**Why.** The law distinguishes between two types of authority: express and implied. Express authority is granted when the person in charge of the business explicitly authorizes the agent to perform specific acts. Implied authority, on the other hand, arises when the person in charge of the business does not explicitly authorize the agent but allows the agent to do something that is necessary for the purpose of the agency.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §190

A4.t:
**Answer.** Express authority is given by words spoken or written, while implied authority is inferred from the circumstances of the case, including things spoken or written, or the ordinary course of dealing.

**Why.** The law defines two types of authority: express and implied. Express authority is explicitly stated through words spoken or written. Implied authority, however, is determined by inference based on the circumstances of the case, which can include things spoken or written, or the ordinary course of dealing.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §187

items.q: What is the primary responsibility of a Judge in a Court of Session?
items.ref: To preside over the court.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A Judge in a Court of Session has the primary responsibility to administer justice according to law.

**Why.** Judges in Courts of Session are required to ensure that all proceedings are conducted fairly and in accordance with the law, ensuring that justice is administered impartially and efficiently.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** The primary responsibility of a Judge in a Court of Session is to preside over the court and dispose of cases.

**Why.** According to the statute, the Court of Session is presided over by a Judge appointed by the High Court, and the Judge is responsible for the disposal of cases within the court.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §8

A3.t:
**Answer.** The Judge must ensure that the trial is conducted according to law.

**Why.** The Judge's duty is to conduct the trial in accordance with the law. This ensures that the proceedings follow the established legal framework.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §415

A4.t:
**Answer.** The Judge must ensure that the Court of Session has an expeditious and proper disposal of cases.

**Why.** The duty of the Judge is to ensure that the Court of Session disposes of cases properly and expeditiously. This responsibility is placed on the Judge who presides over the Court of Session.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §529

items.q: What is the primary responsibility of the Judge on the date fixed for taking evidence in support of the prosecution?
items.ref: The Judge shall proceed to take all such evidence as may be produced in support of the prosecution.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The Judge shall ensure that the evidence is taken in a fair and orderly manner.

**Why.** This ensures that the trial process is conducted justly and that all parties have an opportunity to present their case effectively.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §54

A2.t:
**Answer.** The Judge shall proceed to take all such evidence as may be produced in support of the prosecution.

**Why.** This responsibility ensures that the judicial process moves forward systematically, allowing the prosecution to present its case fully and efficiently.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §254

A3.t:
**Answer.** The Judge must ensure that the accused is present and that the prosecution witnesses are called to give evidence.

**Why.** The Judge has a duty to ensure that the accused appears before the Court on the date set for taking evidence. Furthermore, the Judge must also ensure that the prosecution witnesses are called to give their evidence.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §275

A4.t:
**Answer.** The Judge must take all evidence that is produced in support of the prosecution.

**Why.** The Judge is required to take all evidence that is produced in support of the prosecution on the date fixed for the examination of witnesses. This action is mandatory regardless of the method used for recording the evidence.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §254

items.q: What is the principle governing the apportionment of relief or compensation obtained in a suit under the Indian Contract Act, 1872?
items.ref: The principle is that the relief or compensation shall be dealt with according to the respective interests of the bailor and the bailee.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The relief or compensation obtained in a suit shall be apportioned among the parties in accordance with their respective rights and interests.

**Why.** This principle ensures that each party receives the appropriate share of the relief or compensation based on their contribution or entitlement, promoting fairness and justice in the distribution of benefits derived from the contract.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §49

A2.t:
**Answer.** The party who suffered the loss or damage due to the breach of contract is entitled to receive compensation.

**Why.** The principle is that the party suffering the loss or damage due to the breach of contract is entitled to receive compensation for any loss or damage caused, which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, to be likely to result from the breach of it. This ensures that the aggrieved party is adequately compensated for the harm suffered.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §73

A3.t:
**Answer.** The relief or compensation must be apportioned among all persons who have contributed to the suit.

**Why.** When a suit is filed under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, and relief or compensation is obtained, that relief or compensation must be apportioned among all persons who have contributed to the suit.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §459

A4.t:
**Answer.** Relief or compensation obtained in a suit under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, is deemed to be a debt due to the plaintiff.

**Why.** The law stipulates that any relief or compensation obtained in a suit under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, is deemed to be a debt due to the plaintiff. This status applies regardless of whether the relief or compensation is obtained through a decree or order.

**Source.** The Indian Contract Act, 1872, §74

items.q: What is the procedure for disposing of things found during a search when the search warrant is executed at a location beyond the local jurisdiction of the issuing court?
items.ref: The things found shall be immediately taken before the Court issuing the warrant, unless the location is nearer to the Magistrate having jurisdiction than to such Court.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The things found during a search must be disposed of according to the rules of the court that issued the search warrant, regardless of where the search was conducted.

**Why.** This ensures uniformity and adherence to the jurisdictional authority that granted the search warrant, preventing any potential legal disputes over the handling of seized items.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §56

A2.t:
**Answer.** Such things shall be immediately taken before the Court issuing the warrant, unless such place is nearer to the Magistrate having jurisdiction therein than to such Court, in which case the list and things shall be immediately taken before such Magistrate.

**Why.** The law mandates that items found during a search beyond the local jurisdiction of the issuing court must be presented to the issuing court unless they are closer to a different Magistrate, in which case they should be presented to that Magistrate. This ensures that the proper judicial authority can review and manage the seized items appropriately.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §104

A3.t:
**Answer.** The Magistrate must send the things to the District Magistrate of the local jurisdiction where the search took place, who then has the authority to dispose of them.

**Why.** When a search warrant is executed in a place outside the local jurisdiction of the issuing court, the Magistrate must send all items seized to the District Magistrate of that local area. This District Magistrate is responsible for the final disposal of the items.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §174

A4.t:
**Answer.** If the search warrant is executed at a location beyond the local jurisdiction of the issuing court, the things found must be taken before the issuing court, unless the place is closer to a Magistrate who has jurisdiction, in which case the things must be taken before that Magistrate. This Magistrate must then make an order authorizing the items to be taken to the issuing court.

**Why.** The law mandates that if a search warrant is executed at a location beyond the local jurisdiction of the issuing court, the things found must be taken before the issuing court. However, if the place is closer to a Magistrate who has jurisdiction, the things must be taken before that Magistrate. Furthermore, the Magistrate receiving the items must make an order authorizing their transfer to the issuing court.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §104

items.q: What is the procedure for reading out an order when the person in respect of whom the order is made is present in the Court?
items.ref: The order is read over to the person, or its substance is explained if the person so desires.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The person in respect of whom the order is made shall be called upon to read the order in the presence of the Court.

**Why.** This ensures that the individual affected by the order is aware of it and understands the decision made by the court, thereby upholding the principles of natural justice and transparency.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §154

A2.t:
**Answer.** If the person in respect of whom the order is made is present in the Court, the order shall be read over to him, or if he so desires, the substance thereof shall be explained to him.

**Why.** This ensures that the individual affected by the order is informed of its contents, thereby safeguarding their rights and ensuring transparency in the judicial process.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §131

A3.t:
**Answer.** The order must be read out to the person in whose presence it is made.

**Why.** If the person in respect of whom the order is made is present in the Court, the order must be read out to that person.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §416

A4.t:
**Answer.** The order must be read over to the person in respect of whom it is made, or if that person desires, the substance of the order must be explained to him.

**Why.** When an order is made, the law mandates that if the person affected is present in the Court, the order must be read over to him. Alternatively, if the person prefers, the substance of the order can be explained to him.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §131

items.q: What is the punishment for A, who conspires with B to poison Z and procures the poison and delivers it to B?
items.ref: A is liable to the punishment for murder, which is the same punishment as B.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A and B are both liable to imprisonment for a term of not less than ten years and shall also be liable to a fine.

**Why.** Conspiracy to commit a serious offense, such as poisoning, is treated as an attempt to commit the offense itself, attracting similar penalties. The statute aims to deter such premeditated actions by imposing stringent punishments.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §352

A2.t:
**Answer.** A is guilty of abetting the offence of poisoning and is liable to the punishment for murder.

**Why.** According to the provisions, A, who conspires with B to poison Z and procures the poison and delivers it to B in order that B may administer it to Z, is considered to have abetted the offence in pursuance of the conspiracy. Since the result of the conspiracy is Z's death, A is liable to the punishment for murder.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §49

A3.t:
**Answer.** A shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to a fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that anyone who conspires with another person to commit an offence punishable under this Chapter, and who procures or delivers any noxious thing to that other person, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years and a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §51

A4.t:
**Answer.** A is guilty of abetting the offence of poisoning, and is liable to the punishment provided for the offence of poisoning.

**Why.** A is guilty of abetting the offence of poisoning because he concertedly plans the act with B and then procures and delivers the poison to B for the purpose of using it. This act of abetment is punishable with the punishment for the offence of poisoning.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §49

items.q: What is the punishment for a public servant who engages in trade despite being legally bound not to do so?
items.ref: The public servant shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both or with community service.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A public servant who engages in trade despite being legally bound not to do so is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with a fine, or with both.

**Why.** This provision aims to prevent conflicts of interest and ensure that public servants adhere to their professional obligations. The penalty is designed to be deterrent and commensurate with the nature of the offense, which involves a breach of trust placed in public officials.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §56

A2.t:
**Answer.** Whoever, being a public servant and legally bound not to engage in trade, engages in trade shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both, or with community service.

**Why.** The statute explicitly outlines the penalty for a public servant who violates their duty by engaging in trade, which includes imprisonment, fine, or community service.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §202

A3.t:
**Answer.** The public servant shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that any public servant who trades while prohibited from doing so shall face imprisonment up to two years, along with a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §194

A4.t:
**Answer.** The punishment is simple imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both, or community service.

**Why.** The law mandates that anyone who is a public servant and is legally bound not to engage in trade shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term extending up to one year, or with fine, or with both, or with community service.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §202

items.q: What is the punishment for a public servant who intentionally aids a person in escaping from confinement when the person is subject to imprisonment for a term not extending to ten years?
items.ref: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The public servant is liable to simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with a fine, or both.

**Why.** The statute aims to deter public servants from facilitating the escape of individuals under their custody. This lesser penalty reflects the intent to prevent serious breaches of duty without imposing harsher measures unless the offense is more grave.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §95

A2.t:
**Answer.** The public servant will be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, with or without fine.

**Why.** The statute specifies that if a public servant, legally bound to keep someone in confinement, intentionally aids in their escape, the punishment varies depending on the severity of the offense the person was subject to. In this case, where the person was subject to imprisonment for a term not extending to ten years, the punishment is set at a term not exceeding three years, with or without a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §264

A3.t:
**Answer.** The public servant shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to a fine.

**Why.** A public servant who intentionally aids a person in escaping from confinement when that person is subject to imprisonment for a term not extending to ten years shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §164

A4.t:
**Answer.** The public servant shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

**Why.** The law specifies that if a public servant intentionally aids a person in escaping from confinement, the penalty depends on the nature of the offense. If the person is subject to imprisonment for a term not extending to ten years, the punishment is imprisonment of either description for a term up to three years, or with fine, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §264

items.q: What is the punishment for a public servant who intentionally omits to apprehend a person under sentence of death?
items.ref: Imprisonment for life or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to fourteen years, with or without fine.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A public servant who intentionally omits to apprehend a person under sentence of death is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may be extended to three years, or with a fine, or with both.

**Why.** This provision aims to ensure that public servants fulfill their duty to enforce judicial orders. The specified punishment serves as a deterrent against such omissions.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §95

A2.t:
**Answer.** With imprisonment for life or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to fourteen years, with or without fine.

**Why.** The statute specifies that if a public servant legally bound to apprehend a person under sentence of death intentionally omits to do so, they face a severe punishment to deter such misconduct.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §260(a)

A3.t:
**Answer.** The public servant shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that any public servant who intentionally omits to apprehend a person under sentence of death shall be punished with imprisonment for a term extending up to ten years, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §195

A4.t:
**Answer.** The punishment is imprisonment for life or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to fourteen years, with or without fine.

**Why.** The law specifies that if the person in confinement or who ought to have been apprehended is under sentence of death, the punishment is imprisonment for life or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to fourteen years, with or without fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §260

items.q: What is the punishment for a public servant who negligently allows a person to escape from confinement?
items.ref: The public servant shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

A1.t:
**Answer.** A public servant who negligently allows a person to escape from confinement is liable to imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with a fine or with both.

**Why.** This provision aims to ensure accountability among public servants in maintaining security and order. It reflects the duty of public servants to uphold the law and prevent escapes from custody.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, §95

A2.t:
**Answer.** The public servant will be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

**Why.** This provision outlines the penalty for a public servant who negligently allows a person to escape from confinement, emphasizing the importance of adherence to duty and the potential consequences of negligence in such roles.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §261

A3.t:
**Answer.** The public servant shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Why.** A public servant who negligently allows a person to escape from custody or confinement shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term that may extend to two years, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §194

A4.t:
**Answer.** The punishment is simple imprisonment for a term up to two years, or a fine, or both.

**Why.** The law specifies that whoever, being a public servant legally bound to keep a person in confinement, negligently suffers that person to escape shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §261

items.q: What is the punishment for abetment if the act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment and no express provision is made for its punishment?
items.ref: The punishment is the same as the punishment provided for the offence.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The punishment for abetment in such cases shall be the same as provided for the act abetted.

**Why.** When the act abetted is committed and there is no specific provision for the punishment of the abetment itself, the law deems the punishment for abetment to be equivalent to the punishment for the actual crime committed.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** Whoever abets any offence shall, if the act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment, and no express provision is made by this Sanhita for the punishment of such abetment, be punished with the punishment provided for the offence.

**Why.** The law specifies that the abettor should face the same punishment as the principal offender if the abetted act is committed as a result of the abetment and no specific punishment for abetment is mentioned.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §49

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person who abetted the act shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to a fine.

**Why.** If the act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment and no express provision is made for its punishment, the person who abetted it shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §51

A4.t:
**Answer.** The abettor shall be punished with the punishment provided for the offence.

**Why.** The law mandates that if the act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment and no express provision is made for the punishment of such abetment, the abettor shall be punished with the punishment provided for the offence.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §49

items.q: What is the punishment for abetting the committing of mutiny by an officer or soldier in the Indian Armed Forces?
items.ref: Imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

A1.t:
**Answer.** Abetting the committing of mutiny by an officer or soldier in the Indian Armed Forces is punishable with rigorous imprisonment for life, and the offender is also liable to a fine.

**Why.** The punishment reflects the serious nature of undermining military discipline and order. The statute aims to deter such acts by imposing stringent penalties.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §154

A2.t:
**Answer.** Whoever abets the committing of mutiny by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the Indian Armed Forces will be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Why.** The law imposes severe penalties to deter and punish those who encourage or assist in acts of mutiny within the armed forces, recognizing the serious threat such actions pose to national security and discipline.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §160

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment for life, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that any person who abets the committing of mutiny by an officer or soldier in the Indian Armed Forces shall be punished with imprisonment for life, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §154

A4.t:
**Answer.** The abettor shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that whoever abets the committing of mutiny by an officer, soldier, sailor, or airman in the Indian Armed Forces shall face severe penalties. These penalties include death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment up to ten years, along with liability to fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §160

items.q: What is the punishment for attempting to commit an offence punishable with imprisonment for life or other imprisonment, when no express provision is made by this Sanhita for the punishment of such attempt?
items.ref: The person shall be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the imprisonment for life or, as the case may be, one-half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for that offence.

A1.t:
**Answer.** Attempting to commit an offence punishable with imprisonment for life or other imprisonment is punishable with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine, or with both.

**Why.** The law provides that where no specific provision is made for the punishment of an attempt, the attempt shall be punishable with a lesser sentence than the one prescribed for the completed offence, but still within the limits of one year of imprisonment or a fine, or both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §105

A2.t:
**Answer.** The attempt is punishable with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the imprisonment for life or, as the case may be, one-half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for that offence, or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or with both.

**Why.** The law provides that where no specific provision is made for the punishment of an attempt to commit an offence, the punishment should be equivalent to half the maximum sentence for the completed offence, or half the longest term of imprisonment for similar offences, or a fine, or both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §62

A3.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term provided for the offence, and also liable to a fine.

**Why.** If the attempt is made to commit an offence punishable with imprisonment for life or other imprisonment, but no specific provision exists in this Sanhita for the punishment of such attempt, the person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term extending up to one-fourth part of the longest term provided for the offence, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §51

A4.t:
**Answer.** The person shall be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the imprisonment for life or, as the case may be, one-half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for that offence, or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or with both.

**Why.** The law mandates that anyone who attempts to commit an offence punishable by this Sanhita with imprisonment for life or imprisonment, and who performs an act towards the commission of the offence, shall face punishment. This punishment is defined as imprisonment of any description provided for the offence, for a term up to one-half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for that offence, or alternatively, a fine or both.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §62

items.q: What is the punishment for bribery by treating?
items.ref: Punished with fine only.

A1.t:
**Answer.** The punishment for bribery by treating includes imprisonment for a term which may be extended to seven years and/or a fine.

**Why.** Bribery by treating is considered a serious offense and is subject to a substantial penalty to deter such actions. The specific term and fine are designed to reflect the seriousness of the crime and to act as a deterrent against similar offenses.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, §45

A2.t:
**Answer.** Bribery by treating shall be punished with fine only.

**Why.** The statute specifically differentiates between bribery and treating, imposing a lighter penalty for treating as it involves less severe gratification such as food, drink, entertainment, or provision.

**Source.** The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, §173

A3.t:
**Answer.** The offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and they are also liable to a fine.

**Why.** The law mandates that the offender shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term extending up to seven years. Additionally, the offender is also liable to a fine.
